1. Hard-landing dust is real and new. fx.js:288-291 burst on `hardLand`, particle count scaled by impact speed (n = min(12, 4 + speed*0.3)), gated to 60 m. Closes the visual half of prior gap #4 — but ONLY for falls above 16 m/s, i.e. drops taller than 16^2/44 = 5.82 m.

This is level design conforming to the movement model rather than a new verb, but it is the difference between reachable and stranded.

Bots now crouch: `inp.crouch = seen && dist > 30 && Math.abs(inp.mz) < 0.1 && a.tier >= 3` (bots.js:686) plus a sniper-stance crouch (bots.js:698), and royale.js:133 actorHeight will shrink their capsule because bots load the same Meshy "crouch" clip that sets hasCrouchClip (player.js:309). CAMERA CAVEAT, so it is not miscounted as a movement win: the shake rewrite (coherent two-sine noise, roll term, offset undone before the lerp, single decay at player.js:1274) is genuinely fixed and framerate-independent, but nothing movement-driven raises camShake — the only sources are SHOT_SHAKE on fire (fx.js:170), explosions (fx.js:233) and being hit (fx.js:264). justification:
The prior verdict rested on one sentence: "pulling the trigger produces no camera kick, no view-model movement, no FOV punch and no hitstop, and camShake is written in exactly two places, neither of which is your own gun." That is now false on every clause, verified in code.

FIRING KICK — fx.js:94-95 defines SHOT_SHAKE {pistol .06, smg .045, ar .07, shotgun .20, sniper .26, glauncher .18} and SHOT_FOV {2, 2, 2.5, 5, 5, 4.5}; fx.js:169-172 raises both, gated `if (a === W.player)` so the other 49 actors' shots do not shake you. VIEW-MODEL — weapons.js:439 sets `a.vmKick = 1` on every fire, consumed at weapons.js:271-274 as `weaponMesh.position.z = -vmKick*0.05` decaying at 6/s = a 5 cm slide over 167 ms; nothing else writes weaponMesh.position (only player.js:750, a visibility LOD that explicitly exempts the local player), so it is live.

SHAKE QUALITY — player.js:1256-1268 replaced per-frame `Math.random()` with two incommensurate sine sums (41.3/27.1 and 33.7/19.9 rad/s) plus a roll term `nx*s*0.11` applied after `lookAt` (which zeroes roll), so the shotgun's 0.20 now reads as 1.26° of roll rather than framerate-dependent buzz. The double decay is genuinely gone: `grep -rn "camShake" runtime/` returns setters in fx.js and exactly one decay, player.js:1274, running AFTER the apply.

HITSTOP — ffg_royale3d.js:493-496 scales the frame step to 0.12x while `W.hitstopT > 0`, decremented with the real dt so the freeze is wall-clock constant; fired from fx.js:272 (own kill, 50 ms), :249 (headshot, 30 ms), :234 (explosion within 8 m, 70 ms). Solo only (`if (!W.net)`).

HIT FLASH — this is the item the prompt flagged as previously inert, and it is now real. player.js:284-285 adds a `zFlash` uniform and player.js:292 multiplies it into `diffuseColor.rgb`; fx.js:150-151 captures `material.userData.zFlash` and fx.js:435 drives it. justification:
Four of the prior entry's ten gaps closed, none regressed, so the dimension improved and stays ahead — but "ahead" describes the AI system's DEPTH, not how hard the game plays, and the single largest difficulty lever named in the prior score is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Baseline check first: the prior scorecard was committed AT 791b7806 but was authored against the code BEFORE it (verified: `git show 88941301:...bots.js` line 165 is exactly the HEAL line the prior gap quotes, and line 567 is `const aimY = tp.y + 1.15 + (seen ? (t.vel ? 0 : 0) : 0)` — the flat aim point it quotes). So both 791b7806 and the f5502ecb parity program count as "since". bots.js itself moved only 13 lines in the parity program (`git diff 791b7806 HEAD --stat` → bots.js 13 +/-); everything else bot-facing landed in 791b7806.

WHAT MOVED (verified):
1. Bots can land headshots now. bots.js:581 `HEAD_CHANCE = [0, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.25]`, rolled per-target (bots.js:592) and per-burst (bots.js:689); bots.js:641-642 `const th = t.swimming ? 0.9 : K.actorHeight(t); const aimY = tp.y + th * (bb.aimHigh ? 0.94 : 0.64)`. Standing 1.8 m target → 1.692 m, against weapons.js:544 `isHead = py > feetY + (headY - feetY) * 0.86 && dh < 0.2` = 1.548 m. The old 1.15 m point sat 0.4 m below that threshold and could not reach it at any tier. It is crouch-aware (K.actorHeight shrinks to 1.548 m via royale.js:133) and swim-aware, so it holds at every stance. Tiers 1-2 stay at 0 — the low end of the curve is deliberately preserved.
2. Supply drops are contested. bots.js:57-65 subscribes to `supplyDropLanded` (emitted loot.js:284) and marks any brain within 220 m; bots.js:216-218 scores `s.SUPPLY` at 58 base / 78 for loot_goblin minus 0.12/m, expiring at 90 s; onEnter at bots.js:298, actSupply at bots.js:501-506, dispatch at bots.js:413. The mark is cleared on arrival within 4 m so a bot that gets there second does not orbit empty grass. loot.js's own "contested by nobody" comment is gone.
3. Crouch is wired and not inert. Reset per frame at bots.js:388, set in actCamp (bots.js:571), in actEngage at bots.js:686 `inp.crouch = seen && dist > 30 && Math.abs(inp.mz) < 0.1 && a.tier >= 3`, and by the sniper branch at bots.js:698. Consumed at player.js:897 and paid off at royale.js:167 `if (st.crouching) spread *= CROUCH.spreadMult` (0.62). An AR bot holding 30-45 m now crouch-strafes at 0.45 speed for a 0.62 cone; net spread ~0.82× vs 1.45× standing-walk. Real, not decorative.
4. Difficulty scaling: PARTIALLY closed. bots.js:32 `ROOKIE_TIER_MIX = [18, 16, 10, 4, 1]` (sums to 49, verified) replaces `[8, 12, 14, 10, 5]` for the first three RECORDED matches — gate at bots.js:75. Combined tier-4+5 count drops 15 → 5. Verified live, not inert: W.progress is assigned at boot (hud.js:508 in showMenu, called from ffg_royale3d.js:525) before attachBrain runs (ffg_royale3d.js:361), and `p.career = newCareer(p.career)` (hud.js:1367) always yields a defined career. But it is first-run protection only — `grep -rni "difficulty|sbmm|skillEstimate|casual" runtime/` returns ZERO hits, so from match 4 onward every player forever gets the identical fixed mix.
5. Not in the prior gap list, but a genuine behavioural fix: bots.js:193 `s.FLEE = ... (heals ? 86 : 72)`. FLEE used to require `heals`, so a cracked bot with an empty bag scored 0 and stood trading until it died.

WHAT DID NOT MOVE:
- Shield top-off, the prior "critical". bots.js:194 is byte-identical to the line the prior scorecard quotes (diffed both revisions above). Actors still spawn `shield: 0` (player.js:56). At hp 100 / shield 0 the first clause needs hp<80 and the second needs hp<60, so a healthy bot carrying six minis scores HEAL = 0. Current asymmetry with a legendary AR (30 × 1.32 = 39.6 body): player breaks a bot's 100 EHP in 2.6 hits ≈ 0.5 s of continuous fire; a bot needs ~6 hits through a ~57% burst duty cycle ≈ 1.9 s through the player's 200 EHP. Still ~3.5-4× in the human's favour (prior estimated 4-6×; the headshot fix took the edge off, the dominant term is untouched).
- Pathfinding. `grep -rni "navmesh|pathfind|astar|waypoint" runtime/` → zero hits. moveToward (bots.js:444-461) is unchanged: straight-line steer, hop when support 1.4 m ahead is 0.55-2.2 m up (bots.js:454) against a jump apex of 7.8²/(2×22) = 1.38 m, and a stuck reroute to `randNear(W, a, 25)` at bots.js:458. - Personality depth. rotator is still exactly two decisions (bots.js:106 hot-drop, bots.js:211 PUSH eligibility); loot_goblin gained one (SUPPLY 78 vs 58, bots.js:217) for a total of three. Still ~3 observable archetypes across a 49-bot lobby, not 6.

ROOKIE_TIER_MIX is not asserted anywhere — it lives in bots.js and is never exported to sim/royale.js, so nothing would catch it if it stopped summing to 49 and the tier draw at bots.js:80 (`/ 49 * mix.reduce(...)`) skewed. A synchronous `fastForward` harness now exists (ffg_royale3d.js:537, drives botsMod.update at 1/30 s), but it is a browser-only `window.__LC__` hook with no test calling it.

CONTEXT SHIFT: net.js:5-11 cut the human cap from 8 to 4 (Supabase Realtime H² message billing). Bots are now 46 of 50 slots even in a full friend lobby — this dimension carries more of the product than it did at the prior score, not less.

The change gave the HUMAN a walk-behind-cover option during an 8s medkit (CONSUMABLES.medkit useS: 8, royale.js:100) that no bot uses — a fresh asymmetry in the player's favour, and it leaves every healing bot a stationary target for 2-8s in the open with crouch cleared.

Bots can never earn the first-shot accuracy bonus except with a sniper. royale.js:171 grants a 0.15x spread multiplier only when speed < 0.6 and >0.5s since the last shot; actEngage unconditionally writes a strafe at bots.js:629 (`inp.mx = bb.strafeDir * ...`), so every AR/SMG/pistol/shotgun bot in the lobby is permanently disqualified. Only the sniper branch (bots.js:698) zeroes mx/mz. The single largest accuracy mechanic in the game is human-only in practice.

inert_or_cancelled: The outbound budget's shed branch in send() is UNREACHABLE. CRITICAL_MSG (net.js:109) lists state, bots, hitYou, died, start, hello, bye, takeover, sync, ev — and those are exactly the nine types ever passed to send() (net.js:48, 88, 265, 289, 345, 414, 501, 526, 544, 586, 588). The only live shedding is the ev-list filter at net.js:533-543, which strips fire/emote from an envelope that is still sent unless it empties.

The budget threshold is wrong by a factor of H, so even the live shed engages ~4x too late. sendBudgetLeft returns Math.max(8, Math.floor(100 / H)) sends/s per client (net.js:123). With H clients each sending at 100/H, and each send billed H (1 send + H-1 receivers), the project total this permits is 100*H = 400 msg/s at H=4. The correct per-client divisor for a 100 msg/s project cap is H^2 (6.25 sends/s at H=4). The file's own header states the H^2 law correctly at net.js:6-8; sendBudgetLeft does not implement it. Consequence in play: at H=4 the host (6 state + ~12 bots + 10 ev = ~28/s) trips the 25/s threshold and sheds, but the three guests (~16/s each) never do; at H=2 the threshold is 50/s and NOBODY ever sheds, which is exactly the room size that goes over the real cap the moment someone shoots.

blocking_parity.item: Stop relaying bot snapshots. Seed the bot brains from the match seed, tick them on a fixed step, and make their LOD independent of per-client positions so all 46 simulate identically on every client — then only human state crosses the wire. Deletes ~12 of the ~36 quiet sends/s at H=4 and removes the 24-actor chunking entirely. This is the same recommendation as the prior score and it is still the single largest term.
blocking_parity.note: Requires bot decisions to be deterministic and position-LOD-free; bots.js currently attaches brains only on the authority (ffg_royale3d.js:358-361). Divergence risk is real and needs a determinism test, not a hand check.

blocking_parity.item: Fix the budget divisor: sendBudgetLeft must return ~100/H^2 sends/s per client, not 100/H (net.js:123). At H=4 that is 6.25, not 25. Also move at least `fire` out of CRITICAL_MSG so the shed branch at net.js:128 stops being dead code, or delete the branch and keep the ev-list filter as the only shed path so the mechanism is honest about what it does.

Decide the transport ceiling. Free Supabase (100 msg/s, 2M/mo) cannot carry a 4-human match even after the bot-relay fix; the options are Supabase Pro (500 msg/s, 5M/mo, ~$25/mo), or WebRTC DataChannel mesh with Supabase demoted to signalling only — which removes per-message cost and cuts latency to direct p2p, but needs a TURN fallback for the meaningful slice of players STUN cannot connect, and TURN is a paid, always-on relay.
blocking_parity.note: MONEY + INFRA CALL. Also brushes the 'no outward network call wanted at this time' constraint: online play already calls Supabase, but a TURN provider is a new third-party dependency. Owner should decide before any further netcode work is scheduled.

blocking_parity.item: Host migration plus a guest-side host watchdog. Today a host who quits leaves every guest in an unwinnable match with frozen, unkillable bots (watchdog gated at net.js:560; leave() at net.js:490). Minimum viable: guests watch for host silence, the lowest surviving peer id promotes itself, attaches brains to every netRemote bot and starts stamping the clock.

Rejoin. Persist {room, slot, seed} on match start, offer RECONNECT on boot with a live session, and have the host invert the takeover it already performs (detach brain, set netRemote) and reply with a full state sync. The host owns all this machinery and only ever runs it in one direction (net.js:408-422).

Finish the squad loop: knock-and-revive (downedAt is already reserved at player.js:56, hp/shield already replicate, and the heal channel is already a timed interruptible interaction that a revive can reuse), a teammate status panel with HP and distance, and a shared post-match squad summary. Costs nothing extra on the wire.
Add a ping/marker system. With no voice and no chat it is the only way squadmates can communicate, it is one small message type on the existing ev envelope, and it adds no third-party dependency.

Suppress hit feedback on teammates: gate the hitMarker emit at weapons.js:577 on the same team check hurtActor uses (player.js:1306), so shooting a squadmate stops confirming a hit that deals no damage.

Make PLAY AGAIN keep the room. ffg_royale3d.js:464 currently calls netMod.leave(W) and starts a solo match, silently dissolving the squad — and contradicting net.js:486-489's own stated reason for where leave() lives. Host re-sends `start` with a fresh seed; guests re-enter.

Derive the lobby roster preview from the real assignment rather than an id sort (net.js:227-235 vs :286), and presence-check the room before committing a randCode() so two hosts cannot silently share a 4-character code (net.js:303-308).

Trust boundary, required BEFORE any public path: restrict start/died/takeover to the host peer id, cap hitYou damage at the weapon's maximum possible roll, require the attacker to be alive and in range, rate-limit per attacker, and fold a periodic host->guest roster reconciliation into the sync path so a dropped elimination self-heals.
blocking_parity.note: Not urgent for code-gated friend rooms, where the shooter-authoritative model is the right trade. Becomes a hard precondition the moment matchmaking is wired.

blocking_parity.item: Decide whether public matchmaking and a server-backed leaderboard are wanted at all. Wiring the existing quickMatch() to a PUBLIC MATCH button is small code, but it multiplies concurrent rooms against the same message cap and requires the trust boundary above; a leaderboard means writing match results to the FFG Supabase registry, which is an additional outward network call.
blocking_parity.note: PRODUCT CALL, and it collides with the stated 'no third-party SDK, tracker or outward network call at this time' constraint. Final Drop carries a Leaderboards tag; matching it is not free here. Note the prior score's CrazyGames inviteLink()/showInviteButton() recommendation is now off the table for the same reason — the shipped ?room= deep link is the constraint-compliant substitute and it works today.

Heaviest frame (50 actors clustered in view): 1,010 calls / 4,456,503 tris / 17.77 ms -> 424 calls / 2,821,168 tris / 8.46 ms. Camera at empty sky: 2,901,932 tris -> 1,801,341 tris in 61 calls. The DPR difference (prior medium=1.5, this run devicePixelRatio=1) is not a confound: I re-ran the prior's own fill-rate test and it still holds — 64x36 = 4.91 ms, 1280x720 = 5.19 ms, 1920x1080 = 5.20 ms. Deleting 99.9% of the pixels and multiplying them 4.5x both change nothing, so resolution cannot explain the delta.

WHAT ACTUALLY LANDED, verified in code and by measurement:
1. Loot distance cull — loot.js:569 `const cull = W.lootCull || 150, cull2 = cull*cull` with a 3D distance test at 570-579. Loot group cost went 505 calls / ~7.3 ms -> 132 calls / 2.79 ms, and only 17,619 of the group's triangles now reach the frame.

Measured consequence: unique texture Sources 202 -> 102, 512x512 textures 143 -> 42, renderer.info.memory.textures 195 -> 70, geometries 591 -> 256. This was the gap tied to the 4 GB-Chromebook rule and it is closed.
3. Tree shadow casting — maps.js:1755 `inst.castShadow = false` now applies to EVERY map-wide instanced prop (trees were the prior's deliberate exception), replaced by a 64-instance near-field caster rebuilt on a 20 m threshold at maps.js:1793-1821. This is most of the 2.90M -> 1.80M empty-sky reduction.
4. Match-build main-thread block — three `await yieldPhase()` (maps.js:315 def; calls at 392, 1665, 1823) plus `renderer.compileAsync` during the loading screen (ffg_royale3d.js:388). Measured with a setTimeout(0) lateness probe over three warm builds: longest contiguous block 135 / 173 / 94 ms, against the prior's single 1,934 ms freeze.

justification:
The prior verdict named two things as decisive: "3D localisation and any recorded sample content." One is now fully built and I verified it running; the other is untouched. That is a genuine two-step move, not a one-step one, because eight of the eleven prior gaps are closed in code and confirmed live — but it is not parity, because the game still ships zero recorded SFX.

I did not take this on faith: I served the game at 127.0.0.1:8791, unlocked the context, emitted one `impact` and read the graph back. Camera was (92.05, 34.06, 0.28); `ctx.listener` read exactly (92.05, 34.06, 0.28), forward (-0.96, -0.29, 0), up (-0.29, 0.96, 0) — orthonormal and pitched. The created panner reported `panningModel:"HRTF"`, `rolloffFactor:0`, position (102.05, 39.06, 10.28) = camera + (10, 5, 10), the exact source offset. Front/back and above/below are now real. `createStereoPanner` appears nowhere in runtime/.

WEAPON-RANGE INFORMATION — CLOSED. `AUDIBLE_M` (audio.js:265) = pistol 220 / smg 200 / ar 320 / shotgun 120 / sniper 520 / launcher 260, keyed off `def.cls` — I checked all six `cls:` values in runtime/sim/royale.js:53-64 and every key matches. Brightness is range-dependent too: `df = 1 - out.__d / maxD` clamped at 0.12 drives the filter start and end frequency (audio.js:287, 294-295), and the rifle crack layer is gated to `< 80 m` (audio.js:305). BEDS, REVERB, LIMITER, MUSIC ROUTING — ALL CLOSED, ALL RUNTIME-VERIFIED. I imported the live module instance in the page, tore the beds down with a phase-menu tick, then ticked phase-match and counted nodes: exactly 3 looping BufferSources at playbackRate 0.35 (storm), 0.55 (forest ambience) and 1.0 (shoreline), plus one HRTF panner positioned at (44.7, 3.0, 89.4) — the exact nearest point on a radius-100 circle from a player at (10, 20), so the storm roar genuinely carries a bearing. Their gains converged to 0.0108 / 0.0342 / 0.0292 with the player at 95 m of a 100 m radius, matching the formulas at audio.js:643, 682 and 701 — live, not inert. Separately I patched the AudioContext prototype before the unlock gesture: exactly 1 ConvolverNode (buffer 19845 samples = 0.45 s, 2 channels — the generated IR from `makeIR`, audio.js:41-49), exactly 1 DynamicsCompressor reading threshold -6, knee 0, ratio 20, attack 0.003, release 0.12 (audio.js:63-66), and exactly 1 MediaElementSource — so music really is inside the graph now (audio.js:142-146) and can be ducked (audio.js:151-157) and thinned at the endgame (`musicIntensity`, audio.js:725-734: mix 0.35 at ≤3 alive, lowpass 1400 Hz at ≤10). Menu music read `__routed:true`, volume 0.450 = musicBase 0.9 × musicVol 0.5, confirming masterVol moved to the master gain and is not squared.

WHY NOT PARITY. `assets/audio/` still contains exactly three files and all three are music: music_menu 4,900,350 B, music_match 5,428,518 B, music_endgame 5,352,438 B = 15,681,306 bytes. I parsed the MPEG frame headers: all three are still MPEG-1 Layer III at 64 kbps, byte-identical sizes and mtimes to the prior score. Zero recorded SFX shipped; every report, impact, footstep and reload is still filtered noise. Final Drop answers with 125 recorded clips totalling 2.59 MB (prior-session manifest research, not re-verified this session) — one sixth of Last Circle's audio payload delivering the entire SFX library. It also carries a voice layer Last Circle has none of: gendered damage grunts at 30 m, jump voices, emote barks. Last Circle emits 47 events and audio handles 35; the 12 unhandled include `emote`, `levelUp` and `useConsumable`, and two of the 35 registered handlers are literal empty functions.

Net: the systems layer is now at or past the benchmark (4-stage reload vs FD's 2 clips, 4-surface impacts, a real brickwall limiter, roof-gated convolution reverb, a continuously positioned storm bed against FD's two storm one-shots, music intensity FD does not appear to have, whiz-by FD does not appear to have). The content layer is not: synth timbre and no voices are audible inside the first ten seconds of play, and 15.68 MB of 64 kbps music is a load-time and quality regression against the benchmark. Slightly behind is the honest read; calling it parity would be scoring the architecture and ignoring what a player actually hears.

Re-verified by reading the current source AND by rendering the shipped build live (Playwright/Chromium SwiftShader, 1280x720, graphics tier "high", seeds deepwood 777 / ashgrid 1234 / isla_viva 42). Six of the prior entry's thirteen gaps are fully closed, five are partially closed, two are untouched.

- Shadow radius. ffg_royale3d.js:165 `SHADOW_EXT = { low: 55, medium: 110, high: 160 }` (was 55/55/70), far 400->600 (:177), normalBias 0.02->0.04 (:185). Live probe returned `shadowExt: 160, shadowMap: 4096`. On a 1600 m map that is still 160 m of 1600, but it is 2.3x the old high tier.
- Foliage actually casts now. maps.js:1792-1822 builds a 64-instance near-caster proxy per foliage mesh, rebuilt inside 110 m when the focus moves >20 m. Live: six caster InstancedMeshes with counts 6/6/3/3/3/3, and a real canopy shadow lands on the snow in my Deepwood frame — with shadowMap disabled the same frame has none.

- Aerial perspective. maps.js:36-41 fog 0.0018/0.0019/0.0020 (was 0.00042/0.00045/0.00052 — 3.8-4.3x) with fog colour set to each map's HORIZON hex (maps.js:326). Live: `fog {d:0.002,c:#9fc7e8}` / `{0.0019,#e7cf98}` / `{0.0018,#7fd4f0}`. My Ashgrid aerial shows the ground genuinely dissolving into the skyline; the prior "horizon as saturated as your feet" is gone.

Parking lots got the same treatment (:886-905). Verified: the Isla Viva volcano road is one continuous ribbon, not a dashed staircase.
- Terrain density. maps.js:364 `SEG = 300` (was 220): 5.33 m/vertex and 180,000 triangles, still one draw call (was 7.27 m and 96,800).
- Ground clutter. maps.js:1832-1875: 1,400 instanced cross-quad tufts in a 55 m ring, biome-tinted at 0.82x the ground colour, one draw call, refreshed on a 0.75 s / 10 m gate. Visible in every ground frame I captured — the empty near-field is filled.

Live: they render mid-grey, not the solid black triangles the prior entry photographed.
- Emissive props feed bloom. maps.js:1647-1659: lamp heads (#ffe9a8) and the lighthouse lens (#fff2b0) get emissiveIntensity 2.8 with toneMapped=false. Visible bloom halos around Coco Village's street lamps in my render.
- First local lights in the game's history. maps.js:1678-1701, a fixed pool of 4 PointLights (0xffdc9a, distance 17, decay 2, intensity 6) tracking the nearest lamps inside 60 m at 2 Hz. Live scene dump: 6 lights total (1 Directional, 1 Hemisphere, 4 Point) — was 2.
- Character variety. player.js:266-303 splits each rig by BIND-POSE vertex height into legs/torso/head zones, each with an independently rolled hue, injected via onBeforeCompile behind a shared program cache key. Replaces the single-hue wash. Reads clearly on screen (green vest / tan trousers / black boots).
- Hit flash is no longer inert. fx.js:151 now captures `material.userData.zFlash` and fx.js:436 writes `e.u.value.set(...)`; player.js:284-285 creates that uniform. The old path wrote material.color, which the zone-tint shader divides back out (player.js:292) — it rendered nothing on 100% of actors.
- Shell casings. fx.js:176-183, one brass particle per trigger pull (not per pellet).
- Water material. maps.js:406 roughness 0.13/metalness 0.3 -> 0.30/0.0, killing both the clipped white glint and a metal lobe reflecting a null environment.
- Structure silhouettes. Real apertures cut in house() (maps.js:926-931), hut() (:650-657) and tower() (:698-712) — sill 1.20 m / header from ~2.30 m, sized to the standing eyeline — so buildings are no longer solid prisms.

WHY IT IS NOT PARITY: the two largest gaps are untouched. `grep -rn CSM runtime/` = 0 hits and `grep -rni decal runtime/` = 0 hits. `grep -rn LOD runtime/3d/` returns 9 hits, all of them weapon-geometry LOD (ffg_royale3d.js:145) or animation-mixer LOD (player.js:73) — zero geometric or foliage LOD, zero billboards, against Final Drop's measured 863 LOD entities and its billboard_vegetation_atlas.png. Every structure in the game is still boxes: `grep -c "addBox(" maps.js` = 105, and hut/house/tower/rangerTower/lighthouse/waterTower/steeple/farmland (maps.js:616-1196) are composed exclusively of addBox/addRamp — against 159 prefab templates and 624 render assets of Synty POLYGON art. Six lights against 262. Terrain is still ONE un-chunked PlaneGeometry (maps.js:365). scene.environment is still null everywhere (maps.js:402, 1645; player.js:212; hud.js:309). Water is still one flat plane with no reflection, refraction, foam, depth gradient or underwater state (maps.js:395-422) — my Isla Viva over-water frame is a uniform cyan plate to a hard horizon.

Honest bottom line: the frame no longer contains rendering DEFECTS — it is coherently graded, has real aerial perspective, working near-field shadows, a correct sky, continuous roads and a populated near-field. What remains is an art-CONTENT gap. A side-by-side screenshot still loses to Final Drop, clearly. That is one rung behind, not the "far behind" a broken-looking frame earned.
